(1) the total number of a user’s friends and the number common friends are the main drivers of friendship tie formation, (2) the number of friends does not affect a user’s online activity levels directly, but the number of friends’ activity levels has a strong effect on a user’s activity, and (3) seeding to users with more friends is not always optimal to stimulate users’ online activity levels, but seeding to users with a high activity level of their friends can be more effective.

the more active friends of a person are more important for the person’s own activity levels than his or her own number of friends.

the network structure and the network dynamics are important factors to understand and to influence users’ activities in online social networks.
the network is a key factor in understanding the evolution of online social activities.
the network is not only a platform for information dissemination and content generation but also an important driver of the network’s own evolution.

a structural model of network dynamics is crucial for the design of optimal interventions and the evaluation of the effectiveness of seeding and stimulation strategies within a network.
